title: Lawrence Welk's modern big band
summary: He is glad to hear a big band again.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: No, because -- you know why? The modern bands are coming back. Now, last night they had Lawrence Welk. Did you hear him on Channel Five?

I told you to get him. Yeah. He featured the band, two members in the band, his trombone player, one of his saxes, his clarinetist. He has a big band, and they're playing modern music now. When he first started, he had that champagne style of music, and I didn't like it.

But just like the fellow said up at the Amsterdam, he heard Lawrence Welk, he said, gosh, he's really got it bad now. They sounded great. Four trumpets, four trombones, he had five saxes, three violins, a cello, a bass drum and guitar. That was a solid band. And they played, too. They were very good. I was listening to them all by myself. And I said to myself, I hope oldtime musicians are listening to this.
